title: Sparky the Glow-Worm's Great Escape
markdown:
High in the whispering peaks, clouds like woolly sheep on rocky shoulders, lived wizard Orrin. His cottage clung to the mountainside, windows watchful, a swaying rope bridge to the village. Some wizards are immensely tidy. Orrin was one of them. Spellbooks alphabetized, potion vials in neat spiky script, robes astonishingly free of glitter. Quiet order. Carefulness. His constant companion: Gloss, a sleek raven, midnight feathers preened from Orrin’s shoulder, a sharp intelligent glint. Silent partner in magical and mundane, a feathered shadow with a knack for Orrin’s thoughts.

Orrin also had Sparky, a glow-worm. When happy, Sparky pulsed warm gold, bright enough to read a spellbook on the darkest night: a tiny living lantern. He adored hiding. He had a phenomenal talent for the most inconvenient places imaginable.

One crisp morning Orrin reached for the mossy terrarium, ready for sunrise grooming. Empty. A scan of the tidy cottage revealed nothing. Gloss cawed, worried, echoing the unease in Orrin’s chest. “Not again, Sparky.” Hiking boots. “Where this time?”

The trail, pine-fragrant, wound down to Oakhaven ablaze: the annual Village Fête. Lanterns like dancing stars. Roasted nuts, spiced cider, baked bread. Laughter from stalls and booths. Orrin checked under banners of friendly dragons and smiling flowers, behind prize pumpkins, inside a giant inflatable mushroom. Nothing. Still no Sparky.

“Looking for something, Orrin?” Witch Willow, bright eyes crinkling, playful smile. Squeaky the plump dormouse on her shoulder, nose twitching. Oakhaven’s witch: soothing teas, competitive spirit.

“Sparky. Vanished. A distinct lack of glow. Classic Sparky.”

Willow twinkled. “A vanishing act. Amusing. I seem to have misplaced my lucky thimble. Rolled away during biscuit-judging. Perhaps our quests are destined to intertwine.” A grin. “Grand Fête Scavenger Hunt. Prize: a year’s supply of the finest dandelion wine.”

A tiny spark of competitive fire. “I accept your challenge, Willow. Though I doubt your thimble can out-shine Sparky’s luminescence when he decides to appear. He’s quite the show-off.” Gloss offered an encouraging caw.

The Fête was a whirlwind of friendly competition and delightful chaos. There was Guess the Weight of the Giant Marrow, a vegetable that had opinions about being guessed. Then Most Artistic Cake Decoration, icing roses that would not sit still. And of course the hilarious Splat the Rat, which Pickle would have protested had he been present. Orrin and Willow darted around the bustling grounds, their polite rivalry escalating with each almost-find.

“Found a shiny button!” Willow, a pearly object. “Pretty. Not my thimble’s charm.”

“A rather sparkly pebble.” Smooth grey stone, faint shimmer. “Not quite a glow-worm.”

Gloss took flight, dark wings a blur, circled, landed on the Knotted Rope Challenge tent, cawing insistently toward a peculiar knot of colourful ropes. Orrin followed. Children trying to untangle an enormous bright rope. Nestled deep in a particularly complex knot: a faint warm golden pulse.

“Sparky!” Relief and amused exasperation.

Willow hurried, Squeaky peering. “What a hiding spot. How ever did he get in there?”

Orrin scratched his chin. “He loves a challenge. And he glows brightest when truly content. That pulse is steady. Happy. Not scared.”

A small boy giggled. “Look, mister! The glow-worm is pointing at the loose end. It’s showing us how to undo it!”

Sparky’s light pulsed rhythmically, a tiny beacon. Orrin with his organised mind, Willow with her intuitive understanding, guided the children along the path the glow seemed to highlight. A final heave, delighted giggles, the great rope unfurled, and out tumbled a very pleased Sparky, blinking warm happy light. He had solved the knot-puzzle and then decided to share.

Orrin scooped him into a palm, familiar glow warming his hand. “You certainly know how to make an entrance. A knot-ty problem into a glowing solution.”

Willow clapped, lost thimble forgotten. “Marvelous. Quite the co-conspirator. A little light in the darkness. And my thimble? Biscuit tin. Fancy that.”

Stalls packing. Lanterns a mosaic of gold and ruby. Willow laughed. “For today we’ve found what we were looking for, and more. A bit of magic in the knot-untangling.”

Orrin nodded, a rare smile. “And you are a formidable rival. I shall keep my spellbooks extra organised.”

Gloss gave a soft contented sound. They ascended the swaying rope bridge toward the cottage, stars beginning to prick the inky sky. Sparky pulsed once against Orrin’s palm, as if filing the knot under favourite. Gloss, on the usual shoulder, kept his comments to a look. A glow-worm who preferred puzzles, a raven who had known where to look, and a wizard whose tidy cottage would, by morning, have one terrarium lid that no longer quite latched—Sparky’s opinion, expressed in gold.
audience: children aged 9-10, amusing fantasy story for middle-grade readers
